title: MobileNets: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications

problem.summary: Accuracy-driven network design has made models deeper and more complicated without improving efficiency in size and speed, while real-world applications on computationally limited platforms need timely recognition; prior small-network work mostly optimizes size and ignores latency.
statements: Improvements in accuracy do not necessarily make networks more efficient in size and speed.
Recognition tasks in robotics, self-driving cars and augmented reality must run in a timely fashion on computationally limited platforms.
Many papers on small networks focus only on size but do not consider speed.

evidence.quote: However, these advances to improve accuracy are not necessarily making networks more efficient with respect to size and speed.
In many real world applications such as robotics, self-driving car and augmented reality, the recognition tasks need to be carried out in a timely fashion on a computationally limited platform.
Many papers on small networks focus only on size but do not consider speed.

background.summary: MobileNets builds on depthwise separable convolutions (Sifre, Inception, Xception) and contrasts with compression of pre-trained nets (quantization, hashing, pruning) and distillation; the claimed gap is a model family a developer can size to explicit latency and resource constraints.

relatedWork.name: Depthwise separable convolutions
relatedWork.relation: core prior operation the architecture is built from
relatedWork.quote: MobileNets are built primarily from depthwise separable convolutions initially introduced in [26] and subsequently used in Inception models [13] to reduce the computation in the first few layers.

relatedWork.name: Squeezenet
relatedWork.relation: prior small network using a bottleneck design
relatedWork.quote: Another small network is Squeezenet [12] which uses a bottleneck approach to design a very small network.

relatedWork.name: Knowledge distillation
relatedWork.relation: complementary technique used in the face-attribute and FaceNet use cases
relatedWork.quote: Another method for training small networks is distillation [9] which uses a larger network to teach a smaller network.

relatedWork.name: Network compression
relatedWork.relation: alternative approach of shrinking or compressing pre-trained networks
relatedWork.quote: A different approach for obtaining small networks is shrinking, factorizing or compressing pretrained networks.

evidence.quote: The general trend has been to make deeper and more complicated networks in order to achieve higher accuracy [27, 31, 29, 8].
This paper proposes a class of network architectures that allows a model developer to specifically choose a small network that matches the resource restrictions (latency, size) for their application.

solution.summary: MobileNets is a streamlined architecture built almost entirely from depthwise separable convolutions, together with two global hyper-parameters, width multiplier alpha and resolution multiplier rho, that let a model builder trade latency against accuracy for mobile and embedded applications.
solution.approach: Factorize standard convolutions into a depthwise filter layer and a 1x1 pointwise combination layer, then thin the network with a width multiplier and shrink inputs with a resolution multiplier.
components: depthwise separable convolutions (depthwise 3x3 + pointwise 1x1) with batchnorm and ReLU
width multiplier alpha that thins every layer uniformly
resolution multiplier rho set implicitly via input resolution (224/192/160/128)
28-layer MobileNet body whose first layer is a full convolution
dense 1x1 convolutions implementable directly with GEMM

evidence.quote: MobileNets are based on a streamlined architecture that uses depthwise separable convolutions to build light weight deep neural networks.
We introduce two simple global hyperparameters that efficiently trade off between latency and accuracy.

The MobileNet model is based on depthwise separable convolutions which is a form of factorized convolutions which factorize a standard convolution into a depthwise convolution and a 1 × 1 convolution called a pointwise convolution.
MobileNet uses 3 × 3 depthwise separable convolutions which uses between 8 to 9 times less computation than standard convolutions

experiments.summary: The paper measures ImageNet accuracy against Mult-Adds and parameter count across width/resolution settings, then transfers MobileNets to fine-grained recognition (Stanford Dogs), geo-localization (PlaNet), face attributes, object detection on COCO (SSD and Faster-RCNN) and face embeddings (FaceNet distillation).

evidence.quote: We present extensive experiments on resource and accuracy tradeoffs and show strong performance compared to other popular models on ImageNet classification.
MobileNet is nearly as accurate as VGG16 while being 32 times smaller and 27 times less compute intensive.
For both frameworks, MobileNet achieves comparable results to other networks with only a fraction of computational complexity and model size.

limitations.summary: The authors note accuracy falls off sharply when the model is shrunk too aggressively, that depthwise separable convolutions cost about 1% ImageNet accuracy versus full convolutions, and that depthwise filters need almost no weight decay; detection mAP with a MobileNet backbone also trails larger backbones.
items: Accuracy degrades quickly once the width multiplier reaches 0.25 (50.6% ImageNet accuracy).
Depthwise separable convolutions reduce ImageNet accuracy by about 1% versus a full-convolution MobileNet.
Under SSD and Faster-RCNN, MobileNet backbones obtain lower COCO mAP than Inception V2 and VGG backbones.
Depthwise filters require very little or no weight decay, making training hyper-parameters unusual.

evidence.quote: Accuracy drops off smoothly until the architecture is made too small at α = 0.25.
Depthwise convolution is extremely efficient relative to standard convolution. However it only filters input channels, it does not combine them to create new features.
we found that it was important to put very little or no weight decay (l2 regularization) on the depthwise filters

futureDirections.direction: Release pre-trained MobileNet models in TensorFlow to aid adoption and exploration.
futureDirections.quote: As a next step to help adoption and exploration of MobileNets, we plan on releasing models in Tensor Flow.

equations.name: standard convolution cost
equations.expr: DK * DK * M * N * DF * DF

equations.name: depthwise separable convolution cost
equations.expr: DK * DK * M * DF * DF + M * N * DF * DF

equations.name: cost with width multiplier
equations.expr: DK * DK * aM * DF * DF + aM * aN * DF * DF

applications.detail: MobileNets is explicitly designed for mobile and embedded vision applications with latency and size constraints.
applications.quote: We present a class of efficient models called MobileNets for mobile and embedded vision applications.

applications.domain: robotics, self-driving cars and augmented reality
applications.detail: Named as real-world applications whose recognition tasks must run timely on computationally limited platforms.
applications.quote: In many real world applications such as robotics, self-driving car and augmented reality, the recognition tasks need to be carried out in a timely fashion on a computationally limited platform.

applications.detail: MobileNet serves as the base network for SSD and Faster-RCNN detectors trained on COCO.
A distilled MobileNet compresses a 75-million-parameter face attribute classifier while matching its mean AP at 1% of the Mult-Adds.
The PlaNet geo-localization model is re-trained with the MobileNet architecture.

deploymentClaims: 3x3 depthwise separable convolutions use 8 to 9 times less computation than standard convolutions.
MobileNet is nearly as accurate as VGG16 while being 32 times smaller and 27 times less compute intensive.
The distilled face attribute classifier matches the in-house baseline mean AP while consuming only 1% of the Mult-Adds.
95% of MobileNet computation time is in 1x1 convolutions, which map directly to optimized GEMM routines.

evidence.quote: MobileNet can also be deployed as an effective base network in modern object detection systems.
MobileNet spends 95% of it’s computation time in 1 × 1 convolutions which also has 75% of the parameters as can be seen in Table 2.
MobileNet models can be applied to various recognition tasks for efficient on device intelligence.
